passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute
passages.note: Engrossed text of the instrument Livingston voted on: a tipped-worker carve-out that presupposes and leaves standing the statutory minimum wage.
Bill history page for the same instrument; it prints the chamber tallies and the prime sponsor, but does not name Livingston.
House Third Reading vote detail showing Livingston voting Y on a divided 35-24 roll call, so the near-unanimous rule does not apply.

rows.reasoning: Livingston's only recorded act in these sources is his Y on SCR1040 (2024), which would let the employer of a tipped worker "pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute" while leaving that statutory minimum standing. A subminimum carve-out for one class of worker does not speak to the dimension these rungs order, which is the floor itself: whether to "tie it to the cost of living", "Raise the wage floor to a set higher level", "Keep a modest national wage floor as a baseline", "Hold the wage floor at its current level", or "Remove the wage floor entirely". Every passage is adjacent on V2, so none can support a chair.
